title.zh: 卷一百十六 列傳第六十六: 肅宗代宗諸子
title.en: Volume 116 Biographies 66: Suzong and Daizong's Sons
title.raw: 卷一百十六 列傳第六十六: 肅宗代宗諸子 Volume 116 Biographies 66: Suzong and Daizong's Sons

meta.sourceNote: Body restored from Wikisource juan 116 to match the ChineseNotes chapter heading. The previous Wikisource import used the file number instead of the traditional juan.

sentences.zh: 肅宗皇帝十四子：章敬皇后生代宗皇帝，宮人孫氏生越王係，張氏生承天皇帝，王氏生衛王佖，陳婕妤生彭王僅，韋妃生兗王僴，張美人生涇王侹，裴昭儀生襄王僙，段婕妤生杞王倕，崔妃生召王偲，張皇后生恭懿太子佋、定王侗，宮人生鄆王榮、宋王僖。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong had fourteen sons: Empress Zhangjing bore Emperor Daizong; the palace woman Lady Sun bore Prince of Yue Xi; Lady Zhang bore Emperor Chengtian; Lady Wang bore Prince of Wei Bi; Lady Chen, Jieyu, bore Prince of Peng Jin; Consort Wei bore Prince of Yan Xian; Lady Zhang the Beauty bore Prince of Jing Ting; Lady Pei, Zhaoyi, bore Prince of Xiang Pu; Lady Duan, Jieyu, bore Prince of Qi Chui; Consort Cui bore Prince of Shao Si; Empress Zhang bore Crown Prince Gongyi Shao and Prince of Ding Tong; palace women bore Prince of Yun Rong and Prince of Song Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong had fourteen sons. Empress Zhangjing bore Emperor Daizong; the palace woman Lady Sun bore Prince of Yue Xi; Lady Zhang bore Emperor Chengtian; Lady Wang bore Prince of Wei Bi; Lady Chen, Jieyu, bore Prince of Peng Jin; Consort Wei bore Prince of Yan Xian; Lady Zhang the Beauty bore Prince of Jing Ting; Lady Pei, Zhaoyi, bore Prince of Xiang Pu; Lady Duan, Jieyu, bore Prince of Qi Chui; Consort Cui bore Prince of Shao Si; Empress Zhang bore Crown Prince Gongyi Shao and Prince of Ding Tong; palace women bore Prince of Yun Rong and Prince of Song Xi.

sentences.zh: 越王係，本名儋，肅宗第二子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Xi, original name Dan, was Suzong's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yue Xi, whose original name was Dan, was Suzong's second son.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，封南陽郡王，授特進。

translations.literal: During the Tianbao era, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang commandery and appointed Tejin.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nanyang commandery and appointed Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 至德二年十二月，進封趙王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Zhide, he was promoted to Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Zhide 2 (757), he was promoted to Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年三月，九節度之兵潰於河北，史思明僭號於相州，王師未集，朝廷震駭。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Qianyuan, the armies of the nine frontier commands collapsed in Hebei; Shi Siming usurped a title at Xiang prefecture; the imperial armies had not yet assembled; the court was shaken with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Qianyuan 2 (759), the armies of the nine frontier commands collapsed in Hebei; Shi Siming usurped a title at Xiang prefecture; the imperial armies had not yet assembled; and the court was shaken with alarm.

sentences.zh: 詔以李光弼握兵關東以代子儀。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Li Guangbi to hold command east of the Pass in place of Guo Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Li Guangbi to hold military command east of the Pass in place of Guo Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 光弼請以親賢統師，七月，詔曰：

translations.literal: Guangbi requested that a member of the imperial kin command the army; in the seventh month, an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi requested that a member of the imperial kin command the army; in the seventh month, an edict said:

sentences.zh: 握兵之要，古先為重；

translations.literal: To hold the army's key — from antiquity this has been weighty;
translations.idiomatic: To hold the army's key—from antiquity this has been weighty;

sentences.zh: 命帥之道，心膂攸憑。

translations.literal: in appointing a commander, one relies on the heart and backbone.
translations.idiomatic: in appointing a commander, one relies on the heart and backbone.

sentences.zh: 是知靖難夷兇，必資於金革；

translations.literal: Thus one knows that to quell calamity and subdue the violent, one must rely on arms;
translations.idiomatic: Thus one knows that to quell calamity and subdue the violent, one must rely on arms;

sentences.zh: 總戎授律，實仗於親賢。

translations.literal: to command the host and confer the laws of war truly depends on the imperial kin.
translations.idiomatic: to command the host and confer the laws of war truly depends on the imperial kin.

sentences.zh: 蓋將底寧邦家，保息黎獻者矣。

translations.literal: This is how one will settle the state and household and give the people peace and rest.
translations.idiomatic: This is how one will settle the state and household and give the people peace and rest.

sentences.zh: 朕以薄德，纘承鴻緒，往屬元兇暴亂，中夏不寧。

translations.literal: I, of meager virtue, have succeeded to the great succession; formerly the chief rebel wrought violent disorder and the Central Plain was not at peace.
translations.idiomatic: I, of meager virtue, have succeeded to the great succession; formerly the chief rebel wrought violent disorder and the Central Plain was not at peace.

sentences.zh: 上憑宗社之靈，下藉熊羆之力，由是廓清鹹、洛，拯此生人。

translations.literal: Above I relied on the spirit of the ancestral altars; below I borrowed the strength of bear and tiger; thereby I cleared Xian and Luo and saved these living people.
translations.idiomatic: Above I relied on the spirit of the ancestral altars; below I borrowed the strength of bear and tiger; thereby I cleared Xian and Luo and saved these living people.

sentences.zh: 頃以河朔殘妖，尚稽天討，蛇豕竊依於城堡，塗炭久被於齊氓，朕為人父母，寧忘閔念。

translations.literal: Recently the remnant demons of Heshuo still await Heaven's punishment; serpent and swine steal refuge in walled cities; smearing and burning have long afflicted the people of Qi; I, as father and mother to the people, how could I forget compassionate concern.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the remnant rebels of Heshuo still await Heaven's punishment; serpent and swine steal refuge in walled cities; smearing and burning have long afflicted the people of Qi; I, as father and mother to the people, could not forget compassionate concern.

sentences.zh: 雖好生息戰，每冀其歸降；

translations.literal: Though I love life and would cease from war, I ever hoped they would surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Though I love life and would cease from war, I ever hoped they would surrender;

sentences.zh: 而余孽昧恩，靡聞於悔禍。

translations.literal: yet the surviving remnant knew not grace and gave no sign of repenting their calamity.
translations.idiomatic: yet the surviving remnant knew not grace and gave no sign of repenting their calamity.

sentences.zh: 所以軒後親征於獯鬻，周文致役於昆夷，古之用兵，蓋非獲已。

translations.literal: Therefore the Yellow Emperor personally campaigned against the Xunyu, and King Wen of Zhou levied service against the Kunyi — in antiquity the use of arms was surely not by choice.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Yellow Emperor personally campaigned against the Xunyu, and King Wen of Zhou levied service against the Kunyi—in antiquity the use of arms was surely not by choice.

sentences.zh: 趙王係幼稟異操，夙懷韜略，負東平之文學，蘊任城之智勇。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Xi from youth received an uncommon character and long harbored strategy; he bore the literary learning of Dongping and contained the wisdom and courage of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Xi from youth received an uncommon character and long harbored strategy; he bore the literary learning of Dongping and contained the wisdom and courage of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 性惟忠孝，持愛敬以立身；

translations.literal: In nature he was only loyal and filial, holding love and reverence to establish himself;
translations.idiomatic: In nature he was only loyal and filial, holding love and reverence to establish himself;

sentences.zh: 誌尚權謀，有經通之遠智。

translations.literal: his aim favored stratagem and he possessed far-reaching wisdom that penetrated the classics.
translations.idiomatic: his aim favored stratagem and he possessed far-reaching wisdom that penetrated the classics.

sentences.zh: 知子者父，方有屬於維城；

translations.literal: He who knows his son is the father — only then is there reliance on the wall of the city;
translations.idiomatic: He who knows his son is the father—only then is there reliance on the wall of the city;

sentences.zh: 擇能而授，俾克申於戎律。

translations.literal: choosing the able and entrusting him, so that he may fulfill the laws of war.
translations.idiomatic: choosing the able and entrusting him, so that he may fulfill the laws of war.

sentences.zh: 且兇徒嘯聚，頗歷歲時，惡既貫盈，理當撲滅。

translations.literal: Moreover the violent band has gathered and cried out for quite some time; their evil is full to the brim — reason demands they be struck down and extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the violent band has gathered and cried out for quite some time; their evil is full to the brim—reason demands they be struck down and extinguished.

sentences.zh: 君親有命，可不敬乎！

translations.literal: When lord and parent give command, can one fail to revere it!
translations.idiomatic: When lord and parent give command, can one fail to revere it!

sentences.zh: 俾展龍豹之韜，永清梟獍之類。

translations.literal: Let him deploy the stratagems of dragon and leopard and forever clear the owl-and-tiger kind.
translations.idiomatic: Let him deploy the stratagems of dragon and leopard and forever clear the owl-and-tiger kind.

sentences.zh: 可充天下兵馬元帥，仍令司空、兼侍中、薊國公光弼副知節度行營事。

translations.literal: He may serve as Commander-in-Chief of All Armies and Cavalry under Heaven; Li Guangbi, Minister of Works, concurrently Palace Attendant, Duke of Ji, is further ordered as deputy to manage the frontier command and field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He may serve as Commander-in-Chief of All Armies and Cavalry under Heaven; Li Guangbi, Minister of Works, concurrently Palace Attendant, Duke of Ji, is further ordered as deputy to manage the frontier command and field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 應緣軍司署置，所司準式。

translations.literal: For all military offices to be established in connection with this, the relevant offices shall follow regulation.
translations.idiomatic: For all military offices to be established in connection with this, the relevant offices shall follow regulation.

sentences.zh: 九月，史思明陷洛陽，光弼以副元帥董兵守河陽，王不出京師。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Shi Siming took Luoyang; Guangbi, as deputy commander-in-chief, led troops to hold Heyang; the prince did not leave the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Shi Siming took Luoyang; Guangbi, as deputy commander-in-chief, led troops to hold Heyang; the prince did not leave the capital.

sentences.zh: 十月，下詔車駕親征，諫官論奏乃止；

translations.literal: In the tenth month, an edict was issued for the imperial carriage to campaign in person; remonstrating officials submitted memorials and it was stopped;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, an edict was issued for the imperial carriage to campaign in person; remonstrating officials submitted memorials and it was stopped;

sentences.zh: 王請行，不許。

translations.literal: the prince requested to go; permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: the prince requested to go; permission was denied.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，改封越王。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, his title was changed to Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year, his title was changed to Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年四月，肅宗寢疾彌留。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Baoying, Suzong lay ill near death.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Baoying 1 (762), Suzong lay ill near death.

sentences.zh: 皇后張氏與中官李輔國有隙，因皇太子監國，謀誅輔國，使人以肅宗命召太子入宮。

translations.literal: Empress Zhang had a rift with the inner official Li Fuguo; because the Crown Prince was regent, she plotted to execute Fuguo and sent men with Suzong's command to summon the Crown Prince into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhang had a rift with the inner official Li Fuguo; because the Crown Prince was regent, she plotted to execute Fuguo and sent men with Suzong's command to summon the Crown Prince into the palace.

sentences.zh: 皇后謂太子曰：「賊臣輔國，久典禁軍，四方詔令，皆出其口。

translations.literal: The Empress said to the Crown Prince: "The traitorous minister Fuguo has long controlled the Forbidden Army; imperial edicts to the four quarters all issue from his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress said to the Crown Prince: "The traitorous minister Fuguo has long controlled the Forbidden Army; imperial edicts to the four quarters all issue from his mouth.

sentences.zh: 頃矯制命，逼徙聖皇。

translations.literal: Recently he forged an edict and forced the transfer of the Sacred Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Recently he forged an edict and forced the transfer of the Sacred Emperor.

sentences.zh: 今聖體彌留，心懷怏怏，常忌吾與汝。

translations.literal: Now the Sacred Body lingers near death, brooding with resentment, and constantly bears ill will toward me and you.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Sacred Body lingers near death, brooding with resentment, and constantly bears ill will toward me and you.

sentences.zh: 又聞射生內侍程元振結托黃門，將圖不軌，若不誅之，禍在頃刻。」

translations.literal: I have also heard that the inner attendant of the Archers' Corps, Cheng Yuanzhen, has allied with the Yellow Gate and intends treason; if we do not execute them, disaster will come within moments."
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that the inner attendant of the Archers' Corps, Cheng Yuanzhen, has allied with the Yellow Gate and intends treason; if we do not execute them, disaster will come within moments."

sentences.zh: 太子泣而對曰：「此二人是陛下勛舊內臣，今聖躬不康，重以此事驚撓聖慮，情所難任。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince wept and replied: "These two men are Your Majesty's meritorious old inner officials; now the Sacred Person is unwell — to further alarm the Sacred Mind with this matter is more than I can bear in conscience.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince wept and replied: "These two men are Your Majesty's meritorious old inner officials; now the Sacred Person is unwell—to further alarm the Sacred Mind with this matter is more than I can bear in conscience.

sentences.zh: 若決行此命，當出外徐圖之。」

translations.literal: If this order is carried through, I should withdraw and plan it at leisure."
translations.idiomatic: If this order is carried through, I should withdraw and plan it at leisure."

sentences.zh: 後知太子難與共事，乃召係謂之曰：「皇太子仁惠，不足以圖平禍難。」

translations.literal: Later, knowing the Crown Prince was difficult to work with, she summoned Xi and said to him: "The Crown Prince is benevolent and mild; he is not enough to plan the clearing of this calamity."
translations.idiomatic: Later, knowing the Crown Prince was difficult to work with, she summoned Xi and said to him: "The Crown Prince is benevolent and mild; he is not enough to plan the clearing of this calamity."

sentences.zh: 復以除輔國謀告之，曰：「汝能行此事乎？」

translations.literal: She then told him the plan to eliminate Fuguo and said: "Can you carry out this affair?"
translations.idiomatic: She then told him the plan to eliminate Fuguo and said: "Can you carry out this affair?"

sentences.zh: 係曰：「能。」

translations.literal: Xi said: "I can."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said: "I can."

sentences.zh: 後令內謁者監段恆俊與越王謀，召中官有武勇者二百余人，授甲於長生殿。

translations.literal: Later she had the Inner Usher Supervisor Duan Hengjun plot with Prince of Yue, summoned more than two hundred inner officials noted for martial valor, and issued armor in the Hall of Long Life.
translations.idiomatic: Later she had the Inner Usher Supervisor Duan Hengjun plot with Prince of Yue, summoned more than two hundred inner officials noted for martial valor, and issued armor in the Hall of Long Life.

sentences.zh: 是月乙丑，皇后矯詔召太子，程元振伺知之，告輔國。

translations.literal: On the yichou day of that month, the Empress forged an edict summoning the Crown Prince; Cheng Yuanzhen learned of it by surveillance and informed Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day of that month, the Empress forged an edict summoning the Crown Prince; Cheng Yuanzhen learned of it by surveillance and informed Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 元振握兵於淩霄門候之，太子既至，以難告。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen held troops at Lingxiao Gate awaiting him; when the Crown Prince arrived, he told him of the difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen held troops at Lingxiao Gate awaiting him; when the Crown Prince arrived, he told him of the difficulty.

sentences.zh: 太子曰：「必無此事。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince said: "There must be no such thing.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince said: "There must be no such thing.

sentences.zh: 聖恙危篤，吾豈懼死不赴召乎？」

translations.literal: The Sacred affliction is grave; how could I fear death and fail to answer the summons?"
translations.idiomatic: The Sacred affliction is grave; how could I fear death and fail to answer the summons?"

sentences.zh: 元振曰：「為社稷計，行則禍及矣。」

translations.literal: Yuanzhen said: "For the sake of the altars of state, if you go, calamity will follow."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen said: "For the sake of the altars of state, if you go, calamity will follow."

sentences.zh: 遂以兵護太子匿於飛龍廄。

translations.literal: He then used troops to protect the Crown Prince and hid him in the Flying Dragon Stable.
translations.idiomatic: He then used troops to protect the Crown Prince and hid him in the Flying Dragon Stable.

sentences.zh: 丙寅夜，元振、輔國勒兵於三殿前，收捕越王及同謀內侍硃光輝、段恆俊等百余人。

translations.literal: On the night of bingyin, Yuanzhen and Fuguo marshaled troops before the Three Halls, seized Prince of Yue and the conspiring inner attendants Zhu Guanghui, Duan Hengjun, and more than a hundred others.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of bingyin, Yuanzhen and Fuguo marshaled troops before the Three Halls, seized Prince of Yue and the conspiring inner attendants Zhu Guanghui, Duan Hengjun, and more than a hundred others.

sentences.zh: 禁系幽皇后於別殿，侍者十數人隨之。

translations.literal: Empress Zhang was confined in a separate hall; a dozen attendants followed her.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhang was confined in a separate hall; a dozen attendants followed her.

sentences.zh: 是日，皇后、越王俱為輔國所害

translations.literal: That day, the Empress and Prince of Yue were both killed by Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: That day, the Empress and Prince of Yue were both killed by Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 係子：建、逌、逾。

translations.literal: Xi's sons: Jian, You, and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's sons were Jian, You, and Yu.

sentences.zh: 建，建中元年十一月，封武威郡王，授殿中監同正員；

translations.literal: Jian: in the eleventh month of the first year of Jianzhong, enfeoffed as Prince of Wuwei commandery and appointed Director of the Palace Domestic Service with Honorary Rank;
translations.idiomatic: Jian: in the eleventh month of Jianzhong 1 (780), he was enfeoffed as Prince of Wuwei commandery and appointed Director of the Palace Domestic Service with Honorary Rank;

sentences.zh: 逌封興道郡王，授殿中監同正員；

translations.literal: You was enfeoffed as Prince of Xingdao commandery and appointed Director of the Palace Domestic Service with Honorary Rank;
translations.idiomatic: You was enfeoffed as Prince of Xingdao commandery and appointed Director of the Palace Domestic Service with Honorary Rank;

sentences.zh: 逾封齊國公，光祿卿同正員。

translations.literal: Yu was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi and made Grand Master for Glorious Happiness with Honorary Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi and made Grand Master for Glorious Happiness with Honorary Rank.

sentences.zh: 承天皇帝倓，肅宗第三子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Chengtian Tan, Suzong's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Chengtian Tan was Suzong's third son.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，封建寧郡王，授太常卿同正員。

translations.literal: During the Tianbao era, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jianning commandery and appointed Minister of Ceremonies with Honorary Rank.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jianning commandery and appointed Minister of Ceremonies with Honorary Rank.

sentences.zh: 英毅有才略，善射。

translations.literal: He was resolute and had talent and stratagem; he excelled at archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was resolute and had talent and stratagem; he excelled at archery.

sentences.zh: 祿山之亂，玄宗幸蜀，倓兄弟典親兵扈從。

translations.literal: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, Xuanzong fled to Shu; Tan and his brothers commanded the imperial guard escorting him.
translations.idiomatic: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, Xuanzong fled to Shu; Tan and his brothers commanded the imperial guard escorting him.

sentences.zh: 車駕渡渭，百姓遮道乞留太子，太子諭之曰：「至尊奔播，吾不忍違離左右，俟吾見上奏聞。」

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage crossed the Wei, the people blocked the road begging to keep the Crown Prince; the Crown Prince instructed them: "The Supreme One is fleeing in distress; I cannot bear to leave his side; wait until I have seen him and reported."
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage crossed the Wei, the people blocked the road begging to keep the Crown Prince; the Crown Prince instructed them: "The Supreme One is fleeing in distress; I cannot bear to leave his side; wait until I have seen him and reported."

sentences.zh: 倓於行宮謂太子曰：「逆胡犯順，四海分崩，不因人情，何以興復？

translations.literal: Tan said to the Crown Prince at the traveling palace: "The rebellious barbarian has violated order; the four seas are shattered; without relying on popular sentiment, how can restoration be achieved?
translations.idiomatic: Tan said to the Crown Prince at the traveling palace: "The rebellious barbarian has violated order; the four seas are shattered; without relying on popular sentiment, how can restoration be achieved?

sentences.zh: 夫有國家者，大孝莫若存社稷。

translations.literal: For one who holds a state, there is no greater filial piety than preserving the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: For one who holds a state, there is no greater filial piety than preserving the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 今從至尊入蜀，則散關已東，非皇家所有，何以維屬人情？

translations.literal: If we now follow the Supreme One into Shu, then east of San Pass will no longer be held by the house — how can we hold the loyalty of the people?
translations.idiomatic: If we now follow the Supreme One into Shu, then east of San Pass will no longer be held by the house—how can we hold the loyalty of the people?

sentences.zh: 殿下宜購募豪傑，暫往河西，收拾戎馬，點集防邊將卒，不下十萬人，光弼、子儀，全軍河朔，謀為興復，計之上也。」

translations.literal: Your Highness should recruit heroes, go temporarily to Hexi, gather troops and horses, muster frontier commanders and soldiers — no fewer than a hundred thousand — with Guangbi and Ziyi bringing their full armies from Heshuo to plan restoration: that is the best plan."
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness should recruit heroes, go temporarily to Hexi, gather troops and horses, muster frontier commanders and soldiers—no fewer than a hundred thousand—with Guangbi and Ziyi bringing their full armies from Heshuo to plan restoration: that is the best plan."

sentences.zh: 廣平王亦贊成之，於是令李輔國奏聞。

translations.literal: Prince of Guangling also approved; thereupon Li Fuguo was ordered to report.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guangling also approved; thereupon Li Fuguo was ordered to report.

sentences.zh: 玄宗欣然聽納，乃分從官、士卒以遣之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong gladly accepted; troops and attendant officials were divided and sent off.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong gladly accepted; troops and attendant officials were divided and sent off.

sentences.zh: 時敗卒膽破，兵仗不完，太子既北上，渡渭，一日百戰。

translations.literal: At that time the defeated soldiers were terror-stricken and their weapons incomplete; once the Crown Prince marched north and crossed the Wei, he fought a hundred battles in a day.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the defeated soldiers were terror-stricken and their weapons incomplete; once the Crown Prince marched north and crossed the Wei, he fought a hundred battles in a day.

sentences.zh: 倓自選驍騎數百衛從，每蒼黃顛沛之際，血戰在前。

translations.literal: Tan himself selected several hundred fierce horsemen to guard him; in every moment of sudden peril he fought in the van, bloodied.
translations.idiomatic: Tan himself selected several hundred fierce horsemen to guard him; in every moment of sudden peril he fought in the van, bloodied.

sentences.zh: 太子或過時不得食，倓涕泗不自勝，上尤憐之，軍士屬目歸於倓。

translations.literal: Sometimes the Crown Prince went without food for hours; Tan wept beyond bearing; the emperor especially pitied him; the soldiers looked to Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes the Crown Prince went without food for hours; Tan wept beyond bearing; the emperor especially pitied him; the soldiers looked to Tan.

sentences.zh: 至靈武，太子即帝位。

translations.literal: At Lingwu the Crown Prince assumed the throne.
translations.idiomatic: At Lingwu the Crown Prince assumed the throne.

sentences.zh: 廣平既為元子，欲以倓為天下兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: Guangling, as eldest imperial son, wished to make Tan commander-in-chief of all armies and cavalry under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Guangling, as eldest imperial son, wished to make Tan commander-in-chief of all armies and cavalry under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 侍臣曰：「廣平王冢嗣，有君人之量。」

translations.literal: Attending ministers said: "Prince of Guangling is heir apparent and has the measure of a ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Attending ministers said: "Prince of Guangling is heir apparent and has the measure of a ruler."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「廣平地當儲貳，何假更為元帥？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Guangling's place is as heir designate — why borrow another as commander-in-chief?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Guangling's place is as heir designate—why borrow another as commander-in-chief?"

sentences.zh: 左右曰：「廣平今未冊立，艱難時人尤屬望於元帥。

translations.literal: Those beside him said: "Guangling is not yet formally invested; in hardship the people look especially to the commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Those beside him said: "Guangling is not yet formally invested; in hardship the people look especially to the commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 況太子從曰撫軍，守曰監國。

translations.literal: Moreover the Crown Prince from the day he is made heir is styled Pacifier of the Army; when he guards the state he is styled Regent.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Crown Prince from the day he is made heir is styled Pacifier of the Army; when he guards the state he is styled Regent.

sentences.zh: 今之元帥，撫軍也，廣平為宜。」

translations.literal: Today's commander-in-chief is the Pacifier of the Army — Guangling is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Today's commander-in-chief is the Pacifier of the Army—Guangling is fitting."

sentences.zh: 遂以廣平為元帥，倓典親軍，李輔國為元帥府司馬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Guangling was made commander-in-chief; Tan commanded the imperial guard; Li Fuguo was made vice marshal of the commander-in-chief's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Guangling was made commander-in-chief; Tan commanded the imperial guard; Li Fuguo was made vice marshal of the commander-in-chief's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時張良娣有寵，倓性忠謇，因侍上屢言良娣頗自恣，輔國連結內外，欲傾動皇嗣。

translations.literal: At that time Lady Liangdi was favored; Tan's nature was loyal and outspoken, and in attending the emperor he repeatedly spoke of Liangdi's self-indulgence; Fuguo linked inside and outside, intending to overturn the heir.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lady Liangdi was favored; Tan's nature was loyal and outspoken, and in attending the emperor he repeatedly spoke of Liangdi's self-indulgence; Fuguo linked inside and outside, intending to overturn the heir.

sentences.zh: 自是，日為良娣、輔國所構，雲「建寧恨不得兵權，頗畜異志。」

translations.literal: From then on, he was daily slandered by Liangdi and Fuguo, who spread word that "Prince of Jianning resented not holding military authority and secretly harbored divergent ambitions."
translations.idiomatic: From then on, he was daily slandered by Liangdi and Fuguo, who spread word that "Prince of Jianning resented not holding military authority and secretly harbored divergent ambitions."

sentences.zh: 肅宗怒，賜倓死。

translations.literal: Suzong was angered and ordered Tan to death.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong was angered and ordered Tan to death.

sentences.zh: 既而省悟，悔之。

translations.literal: Afterward he came to his senses and regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he came to his senses and regretted it.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，廣平王收復兩京，遣判官李泌入朝獻捷。

translations.literal: The next winter, Prince of Guangling recovered the two capitals and sent judge Li Bi to court to present the victory.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter, Prince of Guangling recovered the two capitals and sent judge Li Bi to court to present the victory.

sentences.zh: 泌與上有東宮之舊，從容語及建寧事，肅宗改容謂泌曰：「倓於艱難時實得氣力，無故為下人之所間，欲圖害其兄，朕以社稷大計，割愛而為之所也。」

translations.literal: Bi had old ties with the emperor from the Eastern Palace; speaking at ease of Prince of Jianning, Suzong changed countenance and said to Bi: "Tan truly gave strength in the time of hardship; for no reason he was slandered by men beneath him, said to be plotting harm to his elder brother; for the great plan of the state, I severed affection and did what had to be done."
translations.idiomatic: Bi had old ties with the emperor from the Eastern Palace; speaking at ease of Prince of Jianning, Suzong changed countenance and said to Bi: "Tan truly gave strength in the time of hardship; for no reason he was slandered by men beneath him, said to be plotting harm to his elder brother; for the great plan of the state, I severed affection and did what had to be done."

sentences.zh: 泌對曰：「爾時臣在河西，豈不知其故。

translations.literal: Bi replied: "At that time your servant was in Hexi — how could I not know the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied: "At that time your servant was in Hexi—how could I not know the reason?

sentences.zh: 廣平兄弟，天倫篤睦，至今廣平言及建寧，則嗚咽不已。

translations.literal: The brothers of Guangling were bound by natural affection; even now when Guangling speaks of Jianning he sobs without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers of Guangling were bound by natural affection; even now when Guangling speaks of Jianning he sobs without cease.

sentences.zh: 陛下之言，出於讒口也。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty's words issue from slanderous mouths."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's words issue from slanderous mouths."

sentences.zh: 帝因泣下曰：「事已及此，無如之何！」

translations.literal: The emperor wept and said: "It has come to this; nothing can be done!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and said: "It has come to this; nothing can be done!"

sentences.zh: 泌因奏曰：「臣幼稚時念《黃臺瓜辭》，陛下嘗聞其說乎？

translations.literal: Bi then memorialized: "When your servant was young I recited the Melon-Picking Poem at the Yellow Terrace; has Your Majesty ever heard its story?
translations.idiomatic: Bi then memorialized: "When your servant was young I recited the Melon-Picking Poem at the Yellow Terrace; has Your Majesty ever heard its story?

sentences.zh: 高宗大帝有八子，睿宗最幼。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong had eight sons; Ruizong was youngest.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong had eight sons; Ruizong was youngest.

sentences.zh: 天後所生四子，自為行第，故睿宗第四。

translations.literal: The four sons born to Empress Tian arranged their own order among brothers; thus Ruizong was fourth.
translations.idiomatic: The four sons born to Empress Tian arranged their own order among brothers; thus Ruizong was fourth.

sentences.zh: 長曰孝敬皇帝，為太子監國，而仁明孝悌。

translations.literal: The eldest was Emperor Xiaojing, who as Crown Prince regent was benevolent, bright, filial, and brotherly.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest was Emperor Xiaojing, who as Crown Prince regent was benevolent, bright, filial, and brotherly.

sentences.zh: 天後方圖臨朝，乃鴆殺孝敬，立雍王賢為太子。

translations.literal: Empress Tian was then plotting to hold court; she poisoned Xiaojing and made Prince of Yong Xian crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Tian was then plotting to hold court; she poisoned Xiaojing and made Prince of Yong Xian crown prince.

sentences.zh: 賢每日憂惕，知必不保全，與二弟同侍於父母之側，無由敢言。

translations.literal: Xian daily lived in dread, knowing he could not be preserved; with his two younger brothers he attended their parents' side and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Xian daily lived in dread, knowing he could not be preserved; with his two younger brothers he attended their parents' side and dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 乃作《黃臺瓜辭》，令樂工歌之，冀天後聞之省悟，即生哀湣。

translations.literal: He composed the Melon-Picking Poem at the Yellow Terrace and had musicians sing it, hoping the Empress Tian would hear and awaken, and pity would arise.
translations.idiomatic: He composed the Melon-Picking Poem at the Yellow Terrace and had musicians sing it, hoping Empress Tian would hear and awaken, and pity would arise.

sentences.zh: 辭云：『種瓜黃臺下，瓜熟子離離。

translations.literal: The poem runs: 'Melons are planted beneath the Yellow Terrace; when ripe the fruits hang thick.
translations.idiomatic: The poem runs: 'Melons are planted beneath the Yellow Terrace; when ripe the fruits hang thick.

sentences.zh: 一摘使瓜好，再摘令瓜稀，三摘猶尚可，四摘抱蔓歸。』

translations.literal: One picking leaves the melons fair; a second thins them; a third is yet tolerable; a fourth leaves only the vine in one's arms.'
translations.idiomatic: One picking leaves the melons fair; a second thins them; a third is yet tolerable; a fourth leaves only the vine in one's arms.'

sentences.zh: 而太子賢終為天後所逐，死於黔中。

translations.literal: Yet Crown Prince Xian was finally driven out by Empress Tian and died in Qianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Crown Prince Xian was finally driven out by Empress Tian and died in Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 陛下有今日運祚，已一摘矣，慎無再摘。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty's fortune today has already had one picking — take care there is no second."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's fortune today has already had one picking—take care there is no second."

sentences.zh: 上愕然曰：「公安得有是言！」

translations.literal: The emperor started and said: "How can you, sir, speak such words!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started and said: "How can you, sir, speak such words!"

sentences.zh: 時廣平王立大功，亦為張皇后所忌，潛構流言，泌因事諷動之。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Guangling had achieved great merit and was also envied by Empress Zhang; hidden slander was woven; Bi used the occasion to admonish and move him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince of Guangling had achieved great merit and was also envied by Empress Zhang; hidden slander was woven; Bi used the occasion to admonish and move him.

sentences.zh: 及代宗即位，深思建寧之冤，追贈齊王。

translations.literal: When Daizong took the throne, he deeply pondered Jianning's injustice and posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong took the throne, he deeply pondered Jianning's injustice and posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 大歷三年五月，詔曰：「故齊王倓，承天祚之慶，保鴻名之光。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Dali, an edict said: "The late Prince of Qi Tan received Heaven's felicitous blessing and preserved the great name's radiance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Dali 3 (768), an edict said: "The late Prince of Qi Tan received Heaven's felicitous blessing and preserved the great name's radiance.

sentences.zh: 降誌尊賢，高才好學，藝文博洽，智略宏通。

translations.literal: He lowered his will to honor the worthy, was lofty in talent and loved learning; his arts and learning were broad and harmonious, his wisdom and stratagem grand and penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: He lowered his will to honor the worthy, was lofty in talent and loved learning; his arts and learning were broad and harmonious, his wisdom and stratagem grand and penetrating.

sentences.zh: 斷必知來，謀皆先事，識無不達，理至逾精。

translations.literal: In decision he knew what was coming; in planning he always preceded events; in insight nothing was not reached; in principle he went ever deeper.
translations.idiomatic: In decision he knew what was coming; in planning he always preceded events; in insight nothing was not reached; in principle he went ever deeper.

sentences.zh: 乃者寇盜橫流，鑾輿南幸。

translations.literal: Then when bandits and robbers flowed across the land, the imperial carriage went south.
translations.idiomatic: Then when bandits and robbers flowed across the land, the imperial carriage went south.

sentences.zh: 先聖以宸扆之戀，將侍君親；

translations.literal: The former sage, from love of the imperial seat, was about to serve lord and parent;
translations.idiomatic: The former sage, from love of the imperial seat, was about to serve lord and parent;

sentences.zh: 惟王以宗廟之重，誓寧家國。

translations.literal: only the prince, from the weight of the ancestral temple, swore to give the state and house peace.
translations.idiomatic: only the prince, from the weight of the ancestral temple, swore to give the state and house peace.

sentences.zh: 克協朕誌，載符天時，立辨群議之非，同獻五原之計。

translations.literal: He accorded with my will and matched Heaven's time; he promptly distinguished the error of the many opinions and together offered the plan of the Five Plains.
translations.idiomatic: He accorded with my will and matched Heaven's time; he promptly distinguished the error of the many opinions and together offered the plan of the Five Plains.

sentences.zh: 中興之盛，實藉奇功。

translations.literal: The splendor of restoration truly relied on his singular merit.
translations.idiomatic: The splendor of restoration truly relied on his singular merit.

sentences.zh: 景命不融，早從厚穸，天倫之愛，震惕良深。

translations.literal: His bright mandate did not fuse; early he followed the deep tomb; love within the natural bond shook and grieved the good deeply.
translations.idiomatic: His bright mandate did not fuse; early he followed the deep tomb; love within the natural bond shook and grieved the good deeply.

sentences.zh: 流涕追封，胙於東海，頃加表飾，未極哀榮。

translations.literal: With flowing tears he was posthumously enfeoffed in Donghai; shortly after, honors were added, yet the utmost of mourning glory was not reached.
translations.idiomatic: With flowing tears he was posthumously enfeoffed in Donghai; shortly after, honors were added, yet the utmost of mourning glory was not reached.

sentences.zh: 夫以參舊邦再造之勤，成天下一家之業，而存未峻其等，歿未尊其稱，非所以旌徽烈，明至公也。

translations.literal: To share in the toil of restoring the old domain and completing the enterprise of one family under Heaven, yet in life not raise his rank and in death not exalt his title — this is not how to display heroic virtue and make utmost fairness clear.
translations.idiomatic: To share in the toil of restoring the old domain and completing the enterprise of one family under Heaven, yet in life not raise his rank and in death not exalt his title—this is not how to display heroic virtue and make utmost fairness clear.

sentences.zh: 朕以眇身，纘膺大寶，不及讓王之禮，莫申太弟之嗣，所懷靡殫，邈想逾切，非常之命，寵錫攸宜。

translations.literal: I, in my slight person, have succeeded to the great treasure; I did not attain the rites of yielding the throne; I could not declare the succession of the Grand Younger Brother; what I harbor is not exhausted; distant thought grows ever keener; an extraordinary command, favor and bestowal, is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: I, in my slight person, have succeeded to the great treasure; I did not attain the rites of yielding the throne; I could not declare the succession of the Grand Younger Brother; what I harbor is not exhausted; distant thought grows ever keener; an extraordinary command, favor and bestowal, is fitting.

sentences.zh: 敬用追謚曰承天皇帝，與興信公主第十四女張氏冥婚，謚曰恭順皇后。

translations.literal: Respectfully use posthumous title Emperor Chengtian; perform posthumous marriage with the fourteenth daughter of Princess Xingxin, Lady Zhang; posthumous title Empress Gongshun.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully use posthumous title Emperor Chengtian; perform posthumous marriage with the fourteenth daughter of Princess Xingxin, Lady Zhang; posthumous title Empress Gongshun.

sentences.zh: 有司準式，擇日冊命，改葬於順陵，仍祔於奉天皇帝廟，同殿異室焉。」

translations.literal: The relevant offices shall follow regulation, choose a day for investiture, reinter at Shun Mausoleum, and still enshrine at the Temple of Emperor Fengtian, same hall, separate chamber."
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices shall follow regulation, choose a day for investiture, reinter at Shun Mausoleum, and still enshrine at the Temple of Emperor Fengtian, same hall, separate chamber."

sentences.zh: 衛王佖，肅宗第四子。

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Bi, Suzong's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wei Bi was Suzong's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，封西平郡王，授殿中監同正員。

translations.literal: During the Tianbao era, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiping commandery and appointed Director of the Palace Domestic Service with Honorary Rank.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiping commandery and appointed Director of the Palace Domestic Service with Honorary Rank.

sentences.zh: 早薨。

translations.literal: He died early.
translations.idiomatic: He died early.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年五月，追贈衛王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Baoying, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Baoying 1 (762), he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 彭王僅，肅宗第五子。

translations.literal: Prince of Peng Jin, Suzong's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Peng Jin was Suzong's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，封新城郡王，授鴻臚卿同正員。

translations.literal: During the Tianbao era, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xincheng commandery and appointed Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud with Honorary Rank.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xincheng commandery and appointed Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud with Honorary Rank.

sentences.zh: 至德二年十二月，進封彭王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Zhide, he was promoted to Prince of Peng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Zhide 2 (757), he was promoted to Prince of Peng.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年冬，史思明再陷河洛，關東用兵，人情震懼，群臣請以親王遙統兵柄。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Qianyuan, Shi Siming again took Heshuo; troops were deployed east of the Pass; popular sentiment was shaken with fear; ministers requested that an imperial prince hold military command at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Qianyuan 2 (759), Shi Siming again took Heshuo; troops were deployed east of the Pass; popular sentiment was shaken with fear; ministers requested that an imperial prince hold military command at a distance.

sentences.zh: 三年四月詔曰：

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year, an edict said:

sentences.zh: 古之哲王，宅中禦宇，莫不內封子弟，外建籓維。

translations.literal: The wise kings of antiquity, dwelling at the center and ruling the realm, all enfeoffed sons within and established feudatories without.
translations.idiomatic: The wise kings of antiquity, dwelling at the center and ruling the realm, all enfeoffed sons within and established feudatories without.

sentences.zh: 故周稱百代，抑聞麟趾之美；

translations.literal: Thus Zhou was styled for a hundred generations, and one still hears of the beauty of the Linzhi;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zhou was styled for a hundred generations, and one still hears of the beauty of the Linzhi;

sentences.zh: 漢命六官，亦樹犬牙之制。

translations.literal: Han appointed the six ministers and also set the system of dog-teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Han appointed the six ministers and also set the system of dog-teeth.

sentences.zh: 歷考前載，率由舊章。

translations.literal: Examining former records, all follow the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Examining former records, all follow the old statutes.

sentences.zh: 朕以薄德，纘承鴻緒，屬豺狼未殄，金革猶虞。

translations.literal: I, of meager virtue, have succeeded to the great succession; wolves and jackals are not yet extinguished; arms and armor still give concern.
translations.idiomatic: I, of meager virtue, have succeeded to the great succession; wolves and jackals are not yet extinguished; arms and armor still give concern.

sentences.zh: 賴文武藎臣，協心同德，庶克清於玄昆，期永保於皇圖。

translations.literal: Relying on civil and martial ministers of loyalty, hearts joined in one virtue, I hope to clear the dark north and forever preserve the imperial design.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on civil and martial ministers of loyalty, hearts joined in one virtue, I hope to clear the dark north and forever preserve the imperial design.

sentences.zh: 且授鉞分符，義已先於用武；

translations.literal: Moreover to confer axe and tally — the meaning already precedes the use of arms;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover to confer axe and tally—the meaning already precedes the use of arms;

sentences.zh: 又維城作翰，道方弘於建親。

translations.literal: again to make the wall and the writing brush — the Way is just then enlarged by establishing kin.
translations.idiomatic: again to make the wall and the writing brush—the Way is just then enlarged by establishing kin.

sentences.zh: 咨爾分閫之崇，成予磐石之固。

translations.literal: I charge you, the honored of the divided commands, to complete my bedrock solidity.
translations.idiomatic: I charge you, the honored of the divided commands, to complete my bedrock solidity.

sentences.zh: 彭王僅等，銀潢毓慶，璿萼分輝，忠孝稟於天成，文武稱其備用。

translations.literal: Prince of Peng Jin and others — the silver river brought forth blessing; jade calyx shared radiance; loyalty and filial piety received from Heaven's completion; civil and martial called complete in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Peng Jin and others—the silver river brought forth blessing; jade calyx shared radiance; loyalty and filial piety received from Heaven's completion; civil and martial called complete in readiness.

sentences.zh: 今三秦之地，萬國來庭，誠宜列皇子以建封，崇懿籓而制勝，是資固本，委以臨戎。

translations.literal: Now the land of Three Qins, ten thousand states come to court — truly sons should be arrayed to establish enfeoffment, exalted feudatories regulated to overcome — this supports the root and entrusts them to face the army.
translations.idiomatic: Now the land of Three Qins, ten thousand states come to court—truly sons should be arrayed to establish enfeoffment, exalted feudatories regulated to overcome—this supports the root and entrusts them to face the army.

sentences.zh: 彭王僅可充河西節度大使，兗王僴可充北庭節度大使，涇王侹可充隴右節度大使，杞王倕可充陜西節度大使，興王佋可充鳳翔節度大使。

translations.literal: Prince of Peng Jin may serve as military commissioner of Hexi; Prince of Yan Xian may serve as military commissioner of Beiting; Prince of Jing Ting may serve as military commissioner of Longyou; Prince of Qi Chui may serve as military commissioner of Shaanxi; Prince of Xing Shao may serve as military commissioner of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Peng Jin may serve as military commissioner of Hexi; Prince of Yan Xian may serve as military commissioner of Beiting; Prince of Jing Ting may serve as military commissioner of Longyou; Prince of Qi Chui may serve as military commissioner of Shaanxi; Prince of Xing Shao may serve as military commissioner of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 僅，是歲薨。

translations.literal: Jin died that year.
translations.idiomatic: Jin died that year.

sentences.zh: 子鎮，授太仆卿同正員，封常山郡王。

translations.literal: His son Zhen was appointed Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud with Honorary Rank and enfeoffed as Prince of Changshan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen was appointed Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud with Honorary Rank and enfeoffed as Prince of Changshan commandery.

sentences.zh: 兗王僴，肅宗第六子。

translations.literal: Prince of Yan Xian, Suzong's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yan Xian was Suzong's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 母韋妃，刑部尚書堅之妹。

translations.idiomatic: Though Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji had the benevolence of filial sons, in the end they could not turn back a lord-father's love—alas!

sentences.zh: 孝宣皇帝當屯剝之運，收忠義之心，忍行愛子之刑，終宥奸閹之罪，大雅君子，為之痛心。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoxuan, when fortune was withdrawn and stripped, gathered hearts of loyalty and righteousness; he endured executing a beloved son, yet finally pardoned the crime of treacherous eunuchs — great refined gentlemen were pained at heart for this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoxuan, when fortune was withdrawn and stripped, gathered hearts of loyalty and righteousness; he endured executing a beloved son, yet finally pardoned the crime of treacherous eunuchs—great refined gentlemen were pained at heart for this.

sentences.zh: 張後卒以兇終，固其宜矣。

translations.literal: Empress Zhang finally met a violent end — fitting indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhang finally met a violent end—fitting indeed.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：床簀之愛，人情易惑。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Love of bed and mat — human feeling is easily misled.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Love of bed and mat—human feeling is easily misled.

sentences.zh: 以義制情，哲王令德。

translations.literal: To restrain feeling by righteousness — the wise king's fine virtue.
translations.idiomatic: To restrain feeling by righteousness—the wise king's fine virtue.

sentences.zh: 李侯悟主，韻諧金石。

translations.literal: Marquis Li moved his lord; his rhyme harmonized metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Li moved his lord; his rhyme harmonized metal and stone.

sentences.zh: 褒謚建寧，良堪太息。

translations.literal: Praising and posthumously titling Jianning — truly worth a deep sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Praising and posthumously titling Jianning—truly worth a deep sigh.
